description: Peerages, knighthoods and other honours, the Privy Council, lieutenancies, public appointments, and seats in appointed or indirectly chosen bodies (the Senate of Northern Ireland, Seanad Éireann, the nominated European Parliament of 1973-79, the EU Committee of the Regions, the Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly, the British-Irish Inter-Parliamentary Body), by person. Seats won at elections Civgraph holds are in the election results, not here. Each is dated as its sources date it (a peerage from its letters patent, an honour from the list that published it, a Seanad seat from the Oireachtas membership record), with the precision they support; where a source shows only that it was held by a date, start is null and startBy gives the date. Every entry cites Elliott & Flackes (1999) and a second source. Facts only. Schema: data/schemas/honours.schema.json; see docs/facts-model.md.

honours.title: Senator (elected), Nationalist; Deputy Speaker of the Senate 1948-50
honours.note: Settled from the contemporary press: ARK's list ends his seat in 1969, but he was still a senator in 1971-72. The Belfast Telegraph names Senator Gerry Lennon chairman-designate of the SDLP's alternative assembly (5 October 1971), lists him among the Opposition MPs and senators at Dungannon (22 February 1972) and quotes him as a senator for the Nationalist Parliamentary Party (26 February 1972), as Elliott & Flackes have him Opposition leader in the Senate to 1971. The Senate last sat before Parliament was prorogued on 30 March 1972.
